scenes.name: congestion-shift
scenes.prov:
Manual demo scenario — synthetic data. “Delay shifts the weather”: Hand-set: dry and sunny until 6:15 PM, then a rain band with gusts reaches the New York end. An assumed 75 min mid-route delay pushes arrival into the rain and darkness. Weather and the traffic delay are hand-set on purpose; no weather, routing or traffic API is called (only map tiles load). Route geometry and routed times come from a recorded real Valhalla route captured Sat 4:12 PM EDT, Oct 24. Each point uses conditions at its projected arrival time: departure Sun 3:30 PM EDT + routed drive time plus your assumed 1 h 15 min delay mid-route.

captions.text: Long drives go wrong in predictable ways: low sun in your eyes, a storm at the wrong hour, or darkness arriving before you do.
GlarePilot checks weather and sun glare where, and when, you will actually be driving.
It has two clearly separated modes: real data planning, and manual demo scenarios.
Real-data planning first. Preset: Amherst → Chicago, leaving 8:00 AM tomorrow.
The route and the forecast are retrieved live, right now. Each point is evaluated at its projected arrival time.
The trip summary shows the drive time and the expected arrival.
On the map, the route is colored by sun glare, and animated icons mark forecast trouble spots.
Traffic is not predicted. Instead, you state a delay. Here we assume one extra hour.
The delay card shows the new arrival, and every later point is re-timed against the forecast.
Advice cards turn the conditions along the route into short, specific recommendations.
“When should I leave?” compares the same route departing −3 h … +3 h, using a transparent exposure score.
Lower bars mean less glare, wet road, wind and after-dark exposure. The best option is marked.
Next, manual demo scenarios. They use hand-set synthetic weather on a recorded real route, with no weather or route API calls.
“Delay shifts the weather” (synthetic): an assumed 75-minute delay pushes the arrival into rain and darkness.
“Heavy rain + crosswind” (synthetic): rain and wind icons appear where the hand-set squall crosses the route.
“Snow, fog and night” (synthetic): hand-set snow over the Berkshires, freezing fog near Worcester, all after dark.
“Westbound sunset glare” (synthetic). Now we switch from the 2D overview to the 3D chase preview.
The chase preview is a simulated playback of the planned route. It is not GPS.
Scrolling the wheel previews the road ahead. Return jumps back to the playback position.
Play runs a simulated drive along the planned route.
Free, keyless data: Open-Meteo forecasts · Valhalla/OSRM routing · SunCalc sun position.
A planning aid, not a safety system. Manual demos use hand-set data. Built with Kiro for Hackachusetts 2026.
